outlier.evidence: Ratings 6/7/5/7 sit within two points. Reviewer_ffnZ's 5 is the only negative score. The AC notes 'disagreement between reviewer scores ... although not for the reasons behind those scores': all saw limited novelty and good results.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: Partly rote, despite a claimed 8 hours. The summary copies the paper's conclusion (L283-288). The main review copies L76-78 (typo 'irreverent' included) and L95-96, and turns the review-form prompts into statements, e.g. the authors 'are careful and honest about evaluating both the strengths and weaknesses', though checklist 1(b) answers [No] on limitations. Its concrete points (Figure 1 label, batch composition, text overlap with Wu & Yang) sit in the limitations list, and it engaged after the rebuttal. Its 6 is one of A's three positive scores.

checkable_claims.claim: HAN + Ours gives worse audio parsing than HAN; the method mainly improves visual parsing.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1: audio segment F-score 60.1 (HAN) vs 59.2 (HAN + Ours), event level tied at 51.3; visual segment rises 52.9 to 59.9. Table 2: HAN + CM-S drops audio to 58.1/49.6. L266-268 concede the segment-level audio drop for CM-Co.

checkable_claims.claim: No direct experiment shows that CM-S beats the contrastive learning in MA.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 2 adds CM-S only to MA*, which is MA without its contrastive learning (L223-224). MA* + CM-S (Table 2) equals MA (Table 1) within 1.5 points on all ten metrics. The rebuttal's MA + CM-S table adds 0.8 to 1.7 points, segment level only; checklist 3(c) says no error bars.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper gives no parameter or FLOP count for CM-Co, so its gains may come from extra capacity.
checkable_claims.evidence: The submission reports no parameter or FLOP counts. The rebuttal gives 2.4M (HAN) vs 2.8M (HAN + CM-Co) and shows HAN with 2 or 3 layers (2.9M, 3.5M) below HAN + CM-Co on all five segment metrics: a fair control.

checkable_claims.claim: The text does not say how the weights w in Eq. 3 are computed.
checkable_claims.evidence: L125-127 say only that the model 'can obtain' the attention weights. The rebuttal says they come from MLPs, as in HAN [4].

checkable_claims.claim: In the Figure 2 example the ground truth spans the whole video, so it shows nothing about localisation.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 2: ground-truth violin and cello (visual) and cello (audio) all span 0-10 s. The only difference shown is MA missing visual violin before about 6 s. L277-278 also mention 'guitar events' that the figure does not contain.

checkable_claims.claim: The co-occurrence panel of Figure 1 uses a visual query but labels the output as the audio prediction.
checkable_claims.evidence: The green block takes Q from the visual class features, and the caption says it shows 'segment-wise visual prediction', yet the output reads p̂_t^a. The authors conceded the typo.

rebuttal.evidence: Rebuttal posted 2021-08-10. Reviewer_jrWL (edited 2021-08-15): 'I will increase my rating to 7'. Reviewer_2QRh (edited 2021-08-17): 'I would like to upgrade my rating to 7'. Reviewer_nrEQ (edited 2021-09-01): 'I decide to hold my previous rating of 6'. Reviewer_ffnZ's last edit (2021-07-17) predates the rebuttal, so its 5 is pre-rebuttal; it posted nothing after.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: jrWL got the control it asked for: deeper HAN (2-3 layers, 2.9-3.5M parameters) does not match HAN + CM-Co (2.8M); it also got the distinction from [46]. 2QRh accepted the MA + CM-S table (+0.8 to +1.7, segment level) as evidence that CM-S is complementary, although it had asked whether CM-S is superior to MA's contrastive learning. It also accepted the authors' admission that Eq. 8 adds label noise. The novelty argument (contrastive learning over video pairs rather than frame pairs) did not move nrEQ, who still calls the work 'incremental'.

ac.evidence: 'three positives one mildly negative'. Names 'limited technical novelty' as the main limitation, the solution being a 'combination of variants on previously used building blocks', and concludes 'Although somewhat incremental, the paper deserves publication.' The opening sentences copy Reviewer_ffnZ's summary; the task description copies Reviewer_jrWL's.

main_reasons_for_decision: Three of four reviewers positive after the rebuttal (6, 7, 7; mean 6.25)
Two confidence-5 reviewers raised to 7 after new control experiments
State-of-the-art LLP results on three baselines judged sound; incremental novelty accepted

outlier.evidence: Ratings 4/4/5/6. Reviewer_4KfH's 6 is the only positive score, but its post-rebuttal note sides with the novelty critics ('I would not be upset if the paper was eventually rejected'). No champion.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: 1.5 hours at confidence 3 (the form's 'Math/other details were not carefully checked'). Two generic weaknesses ('Technically sound but not inspiring methodology'; parameters grow with classes) and one question; never edited after the rebuttal. Its 5 counted fully in the mean the AC adopted.

checkable_claims.claim: MA* + CM-S (Table 2) reaches about the same accuracy as MA (Table 1), which weakens the case for CM-S.
checkable_claims.evidence: Segment/event F-scores, MA* + CM-S vs MA: audio 60.4/53.5 vs 60.3/53.6; visual 60.7/56.5 vs 60.0/56.4; audio-visual 55.8/47.5 vs 55.1/49.0; Type@AV 58.9/52.5 vs 58.9/53.0; Event@AV 58.6/51.0 vs 57.9/50.6. MA* is MA without its contrastive learning (L223-224), so CM-S, which the rebuttal calls the main novelty, only matches MA's own contrastive loss.

checkable_claims.claim: Eq. 8 is not a proper contrastive loss, because positives appear in the denominator; the denominator should be multiplied by (1-f).
checkable_claims.evidence: The denominator does sum over all n videos, positives included. That is the standard InfoNCE form (MoCo Eq. 1, the paper's [49]) and the usual multi-positive form, not an error. The authors' reply makes the same point.

checkable_claims.claim: Eq. 7 multiplies tensors whose dimensions do not match: w_t^a is 1xC, the feature 1xd.
checkable_claims.evidence: L127 defines w_t^a in R^{1xC}; Eq. 7 multiplies it by f̂_t^a in R^{1xd} and by ȳ in R^{1xC}. The authors replied that w is 'a scalar' and promised to revise. A notation error, not a result error.

checkable_claims.claim: Eq. 6 does not say how the class-level features become a 1xC prediction.
checkable_claims.evidence: Eq. 6 applies MLP_a to the set of C class features of size d_c with no dimensions given. The rebuttal says a d_c x 1 MLP processes each class.

checkable_claims.claim: CM-Co is similar to Tirupattur et al. (CVPR 2021).
checkable_claims.evidence: The paper says so itself: 'Similar to [46] that explicitly models the relationship between event categories' (L134-135).

checkable_claims.claim: The Figure 2 example is simple: violin and cello are always visible and only cello is audible.
checkable_claims.evidence: All three ground-truth bars in Figure 2 span 0-10 s.

checkable_claims.claim: Model parameters grow linearly with the number of event classes.
checkable_claims.evidence: Eq. 4 learns M_c^a and M_c^v in R^{d x d_c} for every class. The authors conceded: 2.8M parameters now, 6.3M at 500 classes.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_6GpX (edited 2021-09-02): 'After the response, I still learn towards rejection, for the reasons in my original review.' Reviewer_4KfH (edited 2021-09-13): agrees 'the techniques lack novelty' and 'would not be upset if the paper was eventually rejected'; whether its 6 was lowered is not visible. Reviewer_2ihx and Reviewer_aCaK never edited after posting, so their 4 and 5 are pre-rebuttal.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: B received the same novelty paragraph as A (contrastive learning over video pairs rather than frame pairs) and the same MA + CM-S table. Neither moved anyone. B's objections were novelty and motivation, which new numbers cannot answer. The authors conceded 2ihx's Eq. 7 notation and the linear parameter growth. Two of four reviewers never replied.

ac.evidence: 'well-informed reviewers had serious questions as to the novelty of the work and strength of the evaluations'; 'I will go with their overall average score in making my recommendation, but I recognize that this paper is very close to the border.' Two sentences, no own reading.

main_reasons_for_decision: Mean rating 4.75; the AC explicitly took the average
Limited novelty: CM-Co close to Tirupattur et al. [46], CM-S a standard supervised contrastive loss
Evaluation judged weak: CM-S only matches MA's contrastive learning; trivial qualitative example; weak motivation

issues_only_a: Parameter/FLOP confound for CM-Co, answered by a deeper-HAN control (Reviewer_jrWL)
HAN + Ours loses audio accuracy, 60.1 to 59.2 segment F-score (Reviewer_2QRh)
Label noise in Eq. 8 when the shared class sits in different modalities (Reviewer_2QRh); authors agreed

Unexplained MMIL weights in Eq. 3 (Reviewer_ffnZ); mislabelled Figure 1 output and Preliminaries text close to Wu & Yang (Reviewer_nrEQ)

Positives in the Eq. 8 denominator (Reviewer_2ihx), a misreading of standard InfoNCE

shared_issues: Limited novelty: HAN/MA backbone plus class co-occurrence as in [46] plus standard contrastive learning (A: Reviewer_nrEQ, Reviewer_ffnZ, Reviewer_jrWL on [46], AC; B: all four reviewers, AC)
No evidence that CM-S beats MA's own contrastive learning (A: Reviewer_2QRh; B: Reviewer_4KfH, Reviewer_2ihx); both got the same MA + CM-S table
Parameters grow linearly with the number of classes (A: Reviewer_ffnZ; B: Reviewer_aCaK)
Figure 2 example too simple (A: Reviewer_ffnZ; B: Reviewer_6GpX)
Limitations not discussed (A: Reviewer_2QRh, Reviewer_ffnZ; B: Reviewer_2ihx, Reviewer_aCaK); checklist 1(b) answers [No]
Batch composition and size for the contrastive loss (A: Reviewer_nrEQ; B: Reviewer_4KfH)
verdict: Both committees saw the same paper: an incremental combination of known parts (HAN/MA backbone, class co-occurrence as in Tirupattur et al., a supervised contrastive loss) with state-of-the-art numbers on LLP, the only benchmark for the task. Both ACs followed their reviewers' scores. A's AC called the work 'somewhat incremental' but publishable; B's AC took the 4.75 mean and called the paper 'very close to the border'. The split comes from the reviewers and the rebuttal. Two of A's confidence-5 reviewers (Reviewer_2QRh, Reviewer_jrWL) asked for experimental controls; the authors supplied new numbers, and both raised to 7. B's reviewers framed the same weakness as novelty and motivation, which no rebuttal can answer. Nobody in B moved up; the most positive B reviewer (Reviewer_4KfH, 6) sided with the novelty critics after the rebuttal, and a 1.5-hour, confidence-3 review (Reviewer_aCaK, 5) counted fully in the average. The paper supports both readings. The full method beats MA by 0.2 to 3.5 points, and a parameter-matched control rules out capacity as the source of the CM-Co gain. But the component the authors call their main novelty, the cross-video contrastive loss (CM-S), only matches MA's own contrastive loss (MA* + CM-S in Table 2 vs MA in Table 1), and no result has error bars. 4KfH (B) flagged this; 2QRh (A) raised the same gap and accepted a rebuttal table with gains near 1 point. Same facts, different weights, at the border.
